idioms.phrase: Wear your heart on your sleeve
idioms.meaning: To show emotions openly.
idioms.example: He wears his heart on his sleeve.

idioms.meaning: To describe vividly.
idioms.example: Her words painted a picture of home.

idioms.meaning: To resonate emotionally.
idioms.example: The poem struck a chord with me.

idioms.meaning: To express a lot without words.
idioms.example: Her silence spoke volumes.

idioms.meaning: A clever or elegant way of wording.
idioms.example: I admire his turn of phrase.

idioms.meaning: To sense the mood of a group.
idioms.example: A good speaker reads the room.

idioms.meaning: To speak with precision and tact.
idioms.example: Choose your words carefully here.

idioms.phrase: Get straight to the heart of
idioms.meaning: To address the core of something.
idioms.example: She got straight to the heart of the issue.

idioms.meaning: To be memorable.
idioms.example: His speech left a lasting impression.

idioms.meaning: To express a feeling in language.
idioms.example: I can't put my joy into words.
idioms.exampleAr: لا أستطيع التعبير عن فرحي بالكلمات.

idioms.meaning: A witty use of double meaning.
idioms.example: The title is a clever play on words.

idioms.meaning: To establish a mood or style.
idioms.example: The opening line sets the tone.

idioms.meaning: Too great to describe.
idioms.example: Her kindness is beyond words.

idioms.meaning: To develop your own style of expression.
idioms.example: Writers spend years finding their voice.

idioms.meaning: To think carefully before speaking.
idioms.example: In a debate, weigh your words.

idioms.meaning: Persuasive, eloquent speech.
idioms.example: The lawyer has a silver tongue.

idioms.meaning: To hurt emotionally.
idioms.example: Those words cut deep.

idioms.meaning: To express what others feel.
idioms.meaningAr: أن تعبّر عمّا يشعر به الآخرون.
idioms.example: The song gives voice to the youth.

idioms.meaning: To soften what you say (usually negative).
idioms.example: She doesn't mince words.

idioms.phrase: The pen is mightier than the sword
idioms.meaning: Words have more power than force.
idioms.example: History shows the pen is mightier than the sword.
idioms.exampleAr: التاريخ يُثبت أن القلم أقوى من السيف.
